thread:
Carla M.: Heads up - we've got a spike in GPU attach failures in eu-west3 over the last 30m. Many pods stuck with "waiting for device". NVMe temp sensors are spiking in a weird pattern, but fans look normal. Anyone seeing this?
Ben K.: seeing it too. Attach rate down ~40% starting ~1717654200. digging through node logs now.
Alice P.: quick check - janitor/scrub backlog is high in that region (queue depth ~1800). Could be causing write stalls that block attach.
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-attach-failure-rate eu-west3 exceeded threshold (75 failures / 10m).
Ben K.: dmesg excerpt:
```
[1717654260.123] nvme0: I/O 0xabc timed out, qdepth 128
[1717654260.124] nvme nvme0: controller reset
[1717654262.200] sd 0:0:0:0: [sda] Unhandled sense code
```
Ben K.: looks like IOPS starvation -> timeouts -> controller resets.
Dave R.: confirmed. Hotstripe hotset + scrub surge. The janitor scrub currently runs at full concurrency during nightly window; combined with a small set of hot volumes it's hitting write queue limits. When nvme qdepth hits saturation, the kube attach path blocks on IO and the device plugin times out.
Carla M.: what are quick mitigations? We can't keep GPUs idle for hours (cost + customer impact).
Dave R.: short term: throttle scrub concurrency per-host to 2 and reduce per-device scrub batch size. That should drop background write bursts and let attach proceed. Also add a fast-path to prioritize attach IO (io_priority for plugin threads).
Alice P.: I can roll a canary to eu-west3 with scrub_concurrency=2 and scrub_batch=64. Patch is small, will push in 5m.
Ben K.: also gating idea - temp sensor anomaly seems correlated but likely secondary. We saw sensors spike when write queues back up (thermal reporting lag). Not convinced it's a hardware fan failure.
Carla M.: agreed. Run the scrub throttle canary and watch attach rate. If attach recovers, we'll treat sensor spikes as symptom.
ops-bot: deploy-started scrub-throttle-canary eu-west3 by Alice P.
Alice P.: canary applied to 10% of hosts. monitoring dashboards updated.
Ben K.: attach failures dropping already - 75 -> 18 in last 10m. :thumbsup: 
Dave R.: good. Create follow-ups: INFRA ticket to add smarter janitor pacing (workload-aware), and a runtime knob to bump gpu-attach IO priority when attach flow detected. Also schedule a firmware health scan for the cohort as precaution.
Carla M.: assigning: Dave for infra design, Ben for monitoring alerts tuning, Alice for scrub rollout and revert plan. I'll own customer comms if needed.
Ben K.: note on cost: blocked GPUs ~2.5k GPU-minutes so far. If this repeats, we should consider temporary cross-region spill to keep user jobs moving.
Carla M.: noted. For now, keep canary and watch for 30m. Thanks everyone.
ops-bot: [INFO] thread closed by Carla M. after confirmation of recovery.
